paragraphs.text: A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin that converts documents to Markdown so an LLM can read them.
# dsh-markdownize

A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin that converts documents to Markdown so an LLM
can read them.

Models work best with plain text. A PDF, a Word file or a spreadsheet read as
raw bytes is noise to

them. Markdown keeps the structure (headings, lists,
tables, slides, pages) while staying compact an

d easy to read. This plugin
gives the agent a `convert_to_markdown` tool that does that conversion
l

ocally. You can also preview a conversion yourself before anything is sent
to the model.
## What it does

- **`convert_to_markdown` tool.** The model calls it with a local file path
and gets the document ba

ck as Markdown, truncated to `max_chars`
(100,000 by default).
- **Two conversion engines.** You pic

k one on the plugin's page:
- its **own engine**, a pure-JavaScript port of MarkItDown's offline
con

verters, bundled with the plugin and always available;
- **Microsoft MarkItDown** (Python), used whe

n it is installed.
- **Images in DOCX and PPTX.** Embedded images become `[Image N: alt text]`
marke

rs. When the current model accepts images, each image is sent right
after its marker.
- **Debug mode

.** Preview the Markdown a file turns into from the web
composer (**Ctrl+Shift+M**). Nothing is sent

e Markdown a file turns into from the web
composer (**Ctrl+Shift+M**). Nothing is sent to the model.
## Supported formats
| Format | Own engine (JS) | Microsoft MarkItDown |

| PDF | yes (text per page) | yes |
| Word `.docx` | yes | yes |
| PowerPoint `.pptx` | yes (text an

d notes per slide) | yes |
| Excel `.xlsx` | yes (one table per sheet) | yes |
| HTML / HTM | yes |

yes |
| CSV / TSV | yes (as a table) | yes |
| JSON / XML | yes (fenced code block) | yes |
| TXT /

MD | yes (as is) | yes |
| ZIP | yes (each supported file inside) | yes |
| Excel 97 `.xls`, EPUB, J
upyter `.ipynb`, Outlook `.msg` | no | yes |
## Conversion engines
### Own engine (JavaScript)
`convert.js` mirrors MarkItDown's offline converters with Node libraries:

for HTML;
- `jszip` and `fast-xml-parser` for PPTX and ZIP.

It needs no Python, no network and no child processes. The libraries ship
pre-bundled in `vendor/`,

so the plugin has no runtime npm dependencies. This
matters because dsh installs local plugins as `l

ink:` dependencies, and pnpm
never installs a linked package's dependencies.
### Microsoft MarkItDown

MarkItDown is Microsoft's Python
tool for the same job. It gives the reference output and reads a fe

w more
formats. Install it with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The plugin looks for it on `PATH` as `markitdown`, `py -m markitdown`,
`python -m markitdown` or `py

thon3 -m markitdown`. If it lives somewhere else,
such as a virtualenv's `markitdown.exe`, set its c

ommand on the plugin's page.
Use double quotes around paths with spaces.
### Choosing the engine

Open **Plugins → dsh-markdownize**. The page shows which engines were found.
When both are available

ugins → dsh-markdownize**. The page shows which engines were found.
When both are available, choose:

- **Automatic** (the default): MarkItDown when it is found, otherwise the
JavaScript engine.
- **Alw

ays MarkItDown**: conversions fail if it is missing.
- **Always JavaScript**.

The choice and the custom command are saved in
`<dshHome>/storages/dsh-markdownize/settings.json`, t

ogether with the image
settings. They apply to both the tool and debug mode. MarkItDown is detected

once per Host start; press
**Search again** after installing it.
## Images in documents

The JavaScript engine extracts the images embedded in DOCX and PPTX files
(including those inside a

ZIP). Each one leaves a marker where it sat: in the
text for DOCX, after the slide's text for PPTX.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The plugin's page sets what happens next:

- **Send them to the model when it accepts images** (the default). The tool
checks the current model

's declared input modalities, as the harness's
`read_image` does. With an image-capable model, each

image is stored as an
attachment and sent right after its marker. With a text-only model, such as
De

epSeek's, only the markers are sent, followed by a note saying why.
- **Text markers only.** Images

the markers are sent, followed by a note saying why.
- **Text markers only.** Images are never sent.

**Most images per conversion** (1–50, 10 by default) caps what one call sends,
and never exceeds the

harness's own per-message image limit. Images past the
cap keep their marker with a note. The model

can also pass
`include_images: false` to get the markers only; it cannot override the
settings.

Repeated images (a logo on every slide) are sent once. Icons smaller than
32 px on both sides are sk

ipped when they have no alt text. PNG, JPEG, GIF
and WebP are sent; EMF, WMF and TIFF keep a marker

only. Debug mode always
shows markers.

MarkItDown does not extract images, so these settings have no effect while
it is the engine in use.
## Install
The plugin needs no build step and no Python. For a `web` profile:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The dump should show a `# == dsh-markdownize` layer. Then start the client:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

On the `desktop` profile, add it from the app's plugin manager as a local
folder.
## Debug mode (web client)

1. Attach a compatible file to the composer, or mention one with `@`.
2. Press **Ctrl+Shift+M**.

Each compatible attachment and `@file` reference is converted on the Host.
`@file` paths are resolve

d against the Session's workspace. The full output,
with no truncation, is written to `<os tmpdir>/d

sh-markdownize-debug/` and
opened in the right Sidebar preview. A composer notice reports its size,

path
and the engine used.

Nothing is sent to the model, and the draft is left as it was. Images and
unsupported formats are sk

g is sent to the model, and the draft is left as it was. Images and
unsupported formats are skipped.
## Limits and safety

- Only local files: URLs are rejected (use the web tools for those).
- Files are read with the privi

leges of the dsh process.
- Files are capped at 50 MB.
- ZIPs are capped at 200 entries and 50 MB un

compressed, and nest at most one
level deep.
- Tool output is truncated at 100,000 characters by def

essed, and nest at most one
level deep.
- Tool output is truncated at 100,000 characters by default.
